traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 362: Weak: Ronse De Craene says Gesneriaceae floral diagrams cannot be told apart from Scrophulariaceae and Plantaginaceae, all on the 5-merous 2:3 (bilabiate) plan; p. 324 notes Gesneriaceae have the most polysymmetric 5-stamened flowers in Lamiales.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 362: Weak: same passage; the euasterid general formula has 2 median carpels (K5 [C(5) A5] G(2)).

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 326 Gesneriaceae: herbs, shrubs or rarely trees; leaves in a basal rosette or opposite, the two of a pair often unequal; flowers usually irregular, often large and showy; corolla united with an oblique limb, often two-lipped; stamens 4 or 2, often with a staminode; ovary superior to inferior, of one cell with two placentas on its wall; fruit a capsule, rarely a berry. Library 1.0's family is 58% shrubs and 27% herbs. The order (Lamiales) states the stipules and the two carpels.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Gesneriaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Gesneriaceae: its irregular flowers have a two-lipped corolla, read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy bilabiate.
